headline: Crude bombs explode in Dhaka, SRB member injured
summary: Attacks targeted Pallabi Police Station, CID headquarters, and Dhaka University, while a school bus was set on fire in Bhatara.
details: A crude bomb thrown from a flyover exploded inside the Pallabi Police Station compound, injuring an SRB-4 member. Two men on a motorcycle threw the device before fleeing the scene.
Pallabi Police chief Jalal Uddin stated that the attack was intended to spread panic. No arrests have been made in connection with the station attack.
In a separate incident, a cocktail bomb exploded outside the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) headquarters on Bir Uttam Shamsul Alam Road in Malibagh.
Multiple crude bombs also exploded at Dhaka University, including areas near the Senate Building and beneath the TSC metro station.
At Dhaka University, students detained two individuals who were subsequently handed over to the police.
Additionally, a bus belonging to the Jalsiri Cantonment School was set on fire in Bhatara around 6:30 pm.
caption:

Pallabi Police chief Jalal Uddin stated that the attack was intended to spread panic. No arrests have been made in connection with the station attack.

In a separate incident, a cocktail bomb exploded outside the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) headquarters on Bir Uttam Shamsul Alam Road in Malibagh.

Multiple crude bombs also exploded at Dhaka University, including areas near the Senate Building and beneath the TSC metro station.

At Dhaka University, students detained two individuals who were subsequently handed over to the police.

Additionally, a bus belonging to the Jalsiri Cantonment School was set on fire in Bhatara around 6:30 pm.

headline_marked: 6 blasts hit DU campus; [[3 suspects detained]]
headline: 6 blasts hit DU campus; 3 suspects detained
summary: Crude bombs exploded at six different locations across the Dhaka University campus on Tuesday evening, leading to the arrest of three men.
details: Six crude bomb explosions rocked the Dhaka University campus on Tuesday evening around 6:42 pm, targeting multiple locations including the metro rail station and the Senate Building.
Students caught two suspects following a blast beneath the university's metro rail station and handed them over to the Shahbagh Police.
A third suspect was detained near the Nilkhet intersection by university authorities and subsequently handed over to the police.
The detained individuals have been identified as Rezaul Karim (42), Sohel Rana (33), and Najmus Saad (33). They are currently being interrogated by the police.
Other blasts were reported near the Institute of Modern Languages, in front of the University Laboratory School and College, at the Nilkhet intersection, and near the Nilkhet gate.
According to police, several individuals arrived by rickshaw near the 'Mukti O Ganatantra' gate near Nilkhet, detonated the bombs, and attempted to flee.
Dhaka University Proctor Prof Israfil Ratan stated that security surveillance across the campus has been stepped up following the incidents.
caption:
Six crude bomb blasts rocked the Dhaka University campus in a series of evening explosions.

Six crude bomb explosions rocked the Dhaka University campus on Tuesday evening around 6:42 pm, targeting multiple locations including the metro rail station and the Senate Building.

Students caught two suspects following a blast beneath the university's metro rail station and handed them over to the Shahbagh Police.

A third suspect was detained near the Nilkhet intersection by university authorities and subsequently handed over to the police.

The detained individuals have been identified as Rezaul Karim (42), Sohel Rana (33), and Najmus Saad (33). They are currently being interrogated by the police.

Other blasts were reported near the Institute of Modern Languages, in front of the University Laboratory School and College, at the Nilkhet intersection, and near the Nilkhet gate.

According to police, several individuals arrived by rickshaw near the 'Mukti O Ganatantra' gate near Nilkhet, detonated the bombs, and attempted to flee.

Dhaka University Proctor Prof Israfil Ratan stated that security surveillance across the campus has been stepped up following the incidents.
